title: TB specialist visit (phthisiatrician)
what: The doctor checks whether you have tuberculosis and treats it. Often people are sent just for a check.
why: For changes on a chest X-ray, a positive TB skin test, contact with a TB patient, a long cough, or for certificates.
duration: the visit usually takes 20 to 30 minutes; tests take from a few days to a couple of weeks
tell_doctor: Whether you had contact with someone who has TB
Cough, night sweats, weight loss, fever
Whether you have had TB before
HIV, diabetes, or taking steroid medicines
Results of past tests and images

prepare.title: Images
prepare.text: Bring your chest X-ray or CT and TB test results, if you have them.

prepare.title: Sputum
prepare.text: If a sputum test is ordered, it is collected in the morning before eating, in a special container. They will explain how.

prepare.title: Mask
prepare.text: If you cough, wear a mask when you come.

steps: The doctor asks about your complaints and contacts
Looks at your images and test results
May order a CT, a sputum test or blood tests
If needed, prescribes treatment or follow-up
feel: If a skin test is done, a quick injection in the forearm
after: If you do not have TB, you get a written conclusion
If treatment is prescribed, you take it for a long time without missing doses
Your close contacts may need to be checked too
red_flags: Coughing up blood or severe shortness of breath: call your local emergency number

faq.q: If I was sent to a TB specialist, do I have TB?
faq.a: No. Most often it is just a check to rule it out.
Yes. The main thing is to take the medicines for the whole course without gaps.
